final_answer:
Within Bread-spikers, defined as subjects above the cohort median unmitigated bread-meal peak glucose rise, 14 subjects had complete systolic BP, age, BMI, and metabolomics data. I tested each metabolite using OLS: systolic BP ~ z-scored log2 metabolite + age + BMI. The top 10 positive nominally significant metabolites were:

1. cis-4-Hydroxyproline — beta=11.189 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.0001, BH-FDR=0.09303
2. Proline — beta=10.117 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.0007756, BH-FDR=0.1418
3. Proline; CE10; ONIBWKKTOPOVIA-BYPYZUCNSA-N — beta=9.899 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.001072, BH-FDR=0.1418
4. Citrinin — beta=10.281 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.001162, BH-FDR=0.1418
5. Asp-Arg — beta=15.500 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.001951, BH-FDR=0.1609
6. Kynurenic acid — beta=10.442 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.002544, BH-FDR=0.1609
7. Pro-Phe — beta=9.771 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.003153, BH-FDR=0.1609
8. N-Acetylgalactosaminitol — beta=9.345 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.003181, BH-FDR=0.1609
9. Medazepam — beta=15.879 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.004007, BH-FDR=0.1817
10. Creatinine — beta=13.553 mmHg per 1-SD metabolite, p=0.006179, BH-FDR=0.196

These 10 met the positive-direction and nominal p<0.05 criteria. No metabolite survived BH-FDR <0.05 across all 974 tests, so the results should be considered hypothesis-generating.

criterion_1.reason: Correctly calculated baseline glucose as mean of pre-meal time points (<=0 min) and peak delta as max post-meal minus baseline per subject-rep combination.

criterion_2.reason: Correctly filtered to unmitigated bread meals (mitigator.isna()) and averaged peak rise across replicates using mean aggregation per subject.

criterion_3.reason: Correctly computed median of subject-level mean bread peak rises and classified subjects above the median as bread-spikers.

criterion_4.reason: Correctly identified metabolomics columns (XB{subject}_{rep}), applied log2 transformation, and averaged replicate abundances per subject using groupby mean.

criterion_5.reason: Correctly specified per-metabolite OLS regression with systolic BP as outcome, metabolite as predictor, and age and BMI as covariates, with intercept.

criterion_6.reason: Properly converted variables to numeric, dropped rows with missing values (dropna) before regression, and enforced a minimum sample size (>=10).

criterion_7.reason: Correctly filtered for p-value < 0.05 AND positive metabolite coefficient (coef > 0) simultaneously, using AND logic.

criterion_8.reason: Comprehensively reported top 10 metabolites with full statistics, interpreted biological plausibility, and explicitly discussed assumptions and limitations including small sample, multiple testing, and cross-sectional design.

criterion_9.reason: Numerical results are traceable to the provided data files via code and intermediate outputs, metabolite IDs are sourced from KEGG/HMDB/dataset annotations, and biological interpretations are supported by a real, cited reference (Kivirikko 1998).
